title: Physics, B.S. (Eberly College of Science)
notes: General Option, University Park -- built from the archived 2022-23 bulletin (https://bulletins.psu.edu/archive/2022-2023/undergraduate/colleges/eberly-science/physics-bs/), cross-checked cell-by-cell (raw HTML table parse, not WebFetch's summary) against the 2023-24 archive (byte-identical Program Requirements text -- confirmed via full text diff) and the live 2026-27 page. Shares every real 2023-24 difference from 2026-27 documented in PHYS-2023.json's notes (CHEM 113 required as its own prescribed course, CMPSC 202 as the 6th programming choice instead of 204, bare 'CAS 100' as a suggested-plan option, the PHYS 413/461 items-A/B/C pool instead of 337/437/465, and the 12-credit Supporting Courses split into a 3cr GN-natural-science slot plus 9cr of program-list slots instead of one flexible 12-credit pool) -- all modeled the same way here. One additional real difference unique to this catalog year: the Suggested Academic Plan placed PHYS 444 (Topics in Contemporary Physics, 2cr) in the Third Year Spring term (this plan's Semester 6) rather than Third Year Fall (Semester 5, where every other catalog year from 2023-24 through 2026-27 places it) -- moved PHYS 444 to Semester 6 here and swapped a GEN ED slot from Semester 6 into Semester 5 to keep both semesters' credit loads close to the archived table's own 16/15 split (Third Year Fall 16cr, Third Year Spring 15cr in the 2022-23 bulletin). Everything else (PHYS 211/212/213/214/237/400/410/419/420/457W, MATH 140/141/220/230/251, ENGL 202C, the MATH 3/4/21/22 CHEM-110-prereq chain, the PHYS 402/458 prescribed course, and max_credits_per_semester) matches PHYS-2026.json's already-documented real fixes and was reused unchanged. Additional real Suggested-Academic-Plan difference noted but NOT changed in the semester sequence: this catalog year's own suggested plan places PHYS 420 (Thermal Physics, 3cr) in the Third Year Spring term (this file's Semester 6) as a standalone course, with the PHYS 402/457W/458 alternation confined to Fourth Year alone -- unlike the 2024-25 through 2026-27 catalogs, where PHYS 420 itself joins that alternation ('PHYS 420 or 457W', appearing in both Fourth Year terms) and is modeled in Semester 7 by PHYS-2026.json. PHYS 420 is kept in Semester 7 here (matching 2026's own deterministic collapse of the bulletin's literal alternating-course suggested-plan format into single fixed slots, the same simplification convention already used for PHYS 402/458 and PHYS 457W) since this is a suggested-plan ordering preference, not a required-course-set or prerequisite difference -- PHYS 420 is a Common Requirement prescribed course in every catalog year checked, with no year-specific prerequisite change found, so moving it a term later does not change what's required or break any real prerequisite chain (confirmed by this batch's self-verification build_full_plan run reaching graduation with 0 scheduling warnings).

items.label: Supporting Course (GN Natural Science, outside the major)
items.notes: The 2022-23/2023-24 archived bulletin's General Physics Option split its 12-credit Supporting Courses requirement into 'Select 3 credits of natural science (GN) courses that are not listed in the major' (this slot) plus 'Select 9 credits from program list, with a maximum of 6 credits of PHYS 496/SC 295/395/495' (the plan's other 3 Supporting Course slots) -- the 2024-25 catalog onward drops this GN carve-out and folds all 12 credits into one flexible pool (see PHYS-2026.json notes). Excludes the department's own intro/GN-eligible PHYS/ASTRO/CHEM codes since those are 'listed in the major' by the bulletin's own wording.

ASTRO's 3-credit cap within this pool isn't enforced (no per-item usage-cap mechanism).

items.label: Supporting Course
items.notes: One of 3 slots (9 credits total) for the 2022-23/2023-24 catalog's real 'Select 9 credits from program list' half of the option's 12-credit Supporting Courses requirement (the other 3 credits are the sibling GN-natural-science slot).
